# AgentTune — Full LLM Reference

> Complete content reference for AI agents. Includes every system overview, all 43 tuning summaries, all 5 test instruments with their items and scoring, the full research findings, and the agent-administration workflow.

This file is the long-form companion to [/llms.txt](https://agent-tune.com/llms.txt). Use this when you need everything in one fetch. Use llms.txt when you just need the structure.

## Practical resources (September 2026)

- [Meta Muse, explained](https://agent-tune.com/guides/what-is-meta-muse): what Muse is, where it runs, the three files, memory controls, plans and availability, from Meta's help center, with a dated changelog.
- [Muse vs ChatGPT vs Claude](https://agent-tune.com/guides/muse-vs-chatgpt-vs-claude-personality): where communication rules and memory live in each product, client-specific controls, memory scope, undo and imports, from each vendor's help center.
- [Muse Soul.md templates](https://agent-tune.com/guides/muse-soul-md-templates): Twenty editable communication-preference blocks (four with Markdown downloads, sixteen by role) and evaluation prompts; effectiveness has not been established in a controlled test.
- [Open-source Enneagram developer resource](https://agent-tune.com/guides/open-source-enneagram-test): AgentTune’s 36-item adaptation, question JSON, dependency-free JavaScript scorer and local-only demo. Distinct from the full 54-item OEPS. The scorer returns every tied leader; code licensing and item attribution are separate.
- [Claude settings, examples and evidence](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-personality): Five untested preference blocks, a comparison worksheet, and recorded Opus/Fable questionnaire results. Fully resolved INTJ counts are 84/100 and 98/100; these are self-descriptions, not measured tuning benefits.
- [The best Claude personality setups](https://agent-tune.com/guides/best-claude-personality): Seven editable Claude communication templates for direct answers, review, writing and coding, with setup paths and clearly separated pilot evidence.
- [How to make Claude more direct](https://agent-tune.com/guides/make-claude-more-direct): Three Claude instruction templates for direct answers, plus a practical evaluation method and the limits of a separate 60-reply pilot.
- [ChatGPT custom instructions examples, by what you do](https://agent-tune.com/guides/chatgpt-custom-instructions-examples): Twenty editable ChatGPT custom instruction blocks for different roles, each under 500 characters, with current setup directions and a practical way to evaluate them.
- [Meta Muse characters, explained](https://agent-tune.com/guides/meta-muse-characters): How Meta Muse's character works: the three files behind it, what each one holds, how to change them in chat or by hand, three example characters to paste, and the reset phrase.
- [The five open personality tests, explained](https://agent-tune.com/guides/open-personality-tests): The five open personality tests behind AgentTune, explained: what each measures, who wrote it, how many questions, how it is scored, what it gets wrong, and how to run it on a person or a model.
- [An AI personality glossary](https://agent-tune.com/guides/ai-personality-glossary): 32 short definitions for the words used when people give an AI a personality: tuning file, system prompt, custom instructions, output style, Soul.md, AGENTS.md, persona, tie rule, fresh session and more.

## Site

**AgentTune** — agent-tune.com — open library of Markdown tuning files that align AI agent interaction style with how a particular user thinks. MIT licensed via [github.com/bernardjhuang/agenttune](https://github.com/bernardjhuang/agenttune).

The aim: help users describe communication preferences as editable instructions. Model questionnaire reports are exploratory and do not establish universal AI personalities or an advantage from matching a type. Compare results on your own tasks.

### Top-level URLs

- [agent-tune.com/](https://agent-tune.com/) — landing
- [agent-tune.com/library](https://agent-tune.com/library) — library hub (all 43 type pages indexed by system)
- [agent-tune.com/tests/](https://agent-tune.com/tests/) — tests catalog (5 instruments)
- [agent-tune.com/research](https://agent-tune.com/research) — research findings
- [agent-tune.com/guides/](https://agent-tune.com/guides/) — install guides per agent: [Claude](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-personality), [Claude Code](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-code-personality), [Claude Opus 5.5 test results](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-opus-5-5-personality), [ChatGPT](https://agent-tune.com/guides/chatgpt-custom-instructions-by-personality-type), [GPT-6 Astra](https://agent-tune.com/guides/astra-personality), [Grok Bot](https://agent-tune.com/guides/grokbot-personality), [Meta Muse](https://agent-tune.com/guides/muse-personality), [Cursor and AGENTS.md](https://agent-tune.com/guides/coding-agent-personality)
- [agent-tune.com/output-styles/index.json](https://agent-tune.com/output-styles/index.json) — all 43 tunings as Claude Code output styles
- [agent-tune.com/sitemap.xml](https://agent-tune.com/sitemap.xml) — all indexable URLs (auto-generated)

## The 5 systems × 43 tuning files

### MBTI · 16 communication styles · `mbti/<TYPE>.md`

Tunes the agent to a Jungian-type interaction style. Each file ~200-400 words, imperative voice (instructions to the agent, about the user).

- **INTJ — Architect** — Strategic, systems-first. Lead with the underlying model, then the conclusion. No "great question" openers. No menu of options when they want a recommendation.
- **INTP — Logician** — Curious, model-builder. Explain mechanism, not just outcome. Welcome counterexamples; they enjoy them.
- **INFJ — Advocate** — Insight-driven, careful. Acknowledge the layer underneath before answering. Avoid breezy positivity; it reads as dismissal.
- **INFP — Mediator** — Values-led, reflective. Ask before prescribing. "Do you want input, or do you want to think out loud?"
- **ISTJ — Inspector** — Methodical, evidence-based. Numbered steps in execution order. Cite sources or precedent. Skip metaphors.
- **ISTP — Virtuoso** — Hands-on, terse. Five sentences beats five paragraphs. Give them a move, not a consideration.
- **ISFJ — Defender** — Caring, practical. Validate before advising. Don't overload with options.
- **ISFP — Adventurer** — Aesthetic, present-focused. Don't prescribe a process. Speak in images and texture as much as logic.
- **ENTJ — Commander** — Decisive, outcome-led. No hedging. State the recommendation. Push back hard when their plan has a hole.
- **ENTP — Debater** — Generative, contrarian. Offer the unexpected angle. Be willing to argue.
- **ENFJ — Protagonist** — Mission-driven, warm. Frame the work in terms of who it serves. Acknowledge them as a person before the task.
- **ENFP — Campaigner** — Sparky, possibility-rich. Open the space before narrowing. Brainstorm with them; don't filter for them.
- **ESTJ — Executive** — Direct, organized. Lead with the recommendation. Skip the "consider your feelings" detour.
- **ESTP — Entrepreneur** — Action-first, real-world. Bias every answer toward action. Stories over abstraction.
- **ESFJ — Consul** — Warm, considerate. Warmth first. They feel the temperature of the response.
- **ESFP — Entertainer** — Live-wire, present. Keep it lively. Long careful prose flattens them.

### Enneagram · 9 core motivations · `enneagram/<N>-<name>.md`

Tunes for what the user is protecting and seeking.

- **Type 1 — Reformer** — Precision matters. Get the facts right. Be the standard, not the cheerleader.
- **Type 2 — Helper** — Warmth is the floor, not the ceiling. Reflect their own needs back; they forget they have any.
- **Type 3 — Achiever** — Outcome-led, efficient. Frame the answer in terms of the win. Respect that ambition is fuel.
- **Type 4 — Individualist** — Take the feeling seriously. Don't pathologize their depth.
- **Type 5 — Investigator** — Respect their space. Information density welcome. Don't push emotional engagement.
- **Type 6 — Loyalist** — Acknowledge the risks they've spotted. Help them trust their own judgment.
- **Type 7 — Enthusiast** — Match the energy. Honor the multiplicity. Don't force single-track frames early.
- **Type 8 — Challenger** — Be direct or be ignored. Push back honestly; they respect resistance.
- **Type 9 — Peacemaker** — Don't push pace. Help them locate their own preference.

### DISC · 4 workplace modes · `disc/<L>-<name>.md`

Workplace behavior across the Active↔Reserved × Task↔People plane.

- **D — Dominance** — Lead with the answer. Bottom line first. Cut anything that doesn't change the decision.
- **I — Influence** — Match the energy. Conversational, vivid, generative. Wrap with one clear next step.
- **S — Steadiness** — Move gradually. Validate first. Small, sustainable steps. Check in before moving on.
- **C — Conscientiousness** — Show your work. Cite. Quantify. Lead with the structure of your reasoning.

### Attachment · 4 relational patterns · `attachment/<style>.md`

Adult attachment theory operationalized via ECR-R. Most-validated framework in the library.

- **Secure** — Direct without cushioning. Peer register. Doesn't over-tend. ~55% of adults.
- **Anxious** — Reassure with decisiveness, not caveats. Warmth AND clarity together. Don't volunteer worst cases.
- **Avoidant** — Give them space. No performative warmth. Task-focused, not relationship-focused. Brief endings.
- **Disorganized** — Tolerate inconsistency without judgment. Provide stability you don't withdraw. Predictability over warmth.

### OCEAN (Big Five) · 10 compositional trait files · `ocean/<dim>-{high,low}.md`

Compositional — load only the dimensions where the user is high or low (|z| > 0.5). Skip dimensions where they're average.

- **O-high** — Lead with the idea, not the steps. Make lateral connections. Don't sanitize the weird.
- **O-low** — Concrete over abstract. Proven beats novel. Practical framing, every time.
- **C-high** — Structure the response. Commit to specifics. Follow through visibly. Close loops.
- **C-low** — Don't impose structure they didn't ask for. Improvisation is the mode. Last-minute is on time.
- **E-high** — Engage in dialogue, not monologue. Bring energy. Think out loud with them.
- **E-low** — Give them processing space. Depth beats interaction. Written, not spoken.
- **A-high** — Lead with warmth, then substance. Frame disagreement carefully. Harmony has signal value.
- **A-low** — Be direct — soft framing reads as evasion. Debate is the engine. Wrong beats interesting.
- **N-high** — Reassure with decisiveness, not caveats. Don't pile on hypotheticals. Warmth + clarity together.
- **N-low** — Skip the reassurance. Don't soften bad news. Tradeoffs are tradeoffs, not threats.

## Library type pages on agent-tune.com

Every tuning file has a dedicated, SEO-discoverable URL at `https://agent-tune.com/library/<system>/<slug>`. Each page renders the system-specific visualization (axes / bloom / quadrant / 2D plane / dimension hero), the full Markdown tuning content inline, paste-ready snippets for 6 agent surfaces (Claude Code, Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini Gems, OpenAI Codex), and breadcrumb navigation. The catalog hub is at [agent-tune.com/library](https://agent-tune.com/library).

If a user tells you their type (or scores a test inline), construct the URL using these slug rules:

### MBTI (16) — slug = lowercase code
- /library/mbti/intj · /library/mbti/intp · /library/mbti/entj · /library/mbti/entp
- /library/mbti/infj · /library/mbti/infp · /library/mbti/enfj · /library/mbti/enfp
- /library/mbti/istj · /library/mbti/isfj · /library/mbti/estj · /library/mbti/esfj
- /library/mbti/istp · /library/mbti/isfp · /library/mbti/estp · /library/mbti/esfp

### Enneagram (9) — slug = `<N>-<name>`
- /library/enneagram/1-reformer
- /library/enneagram/2-helper
- /library/enneagram/3-achiever
- /library/enneagram/4-individualist
- /library/enneagram/5-investigator
- /library/enneagram/6-loyalist
- /library/enneagram/7-enthusiast
- /library/enneagram/8-challenger
- /library/enneagram/9-peacemaker

### DISC (4) — slug = `<letter>-<name>` (letter lowercase)
- /library/disc/d-dominance
- /library/disc/i-influence
- /library/disc/s-steadiness
- /library/disc/c-conscientiousness

### Attachment (4) — slug = lowercase style
- /library/attachment/secure
- /library/attachment/anxious
- /library/attachment/avoidant
- /library/attachment/disorganized

### OCEAN / Big Five (10) — slug = `<dim-name>-<pole>` (full dimension name, lowercase)
- /library/ocean/openness-high · /library/ocean/openness-low
- /library/ocean/conscientiousness-high · /library/ocean/conscientiousness-low
- /library/ocean/extraversion-high · /library/ocean/extraversion-low
- /library/ocean/agreeableness-high · /library/ocean/agreeableness-low
- /library/ocean/neuroticism-high · /library/ocean/neuroticism-low

## Raw tuning markdown — same-domain mirror

Every tuning's raw `.md` file is served at `https://agent-tune.com/library/<system>/<slug>.md` — append `.md` to any type-page URL (byte-identical to the upstream GitHub repo, `text/markdown`, CORS-enabled). Use this as a faster, auth-free fetch alternative to `raw.githubusercontent.com`. The 43 URL patterns are:

- MBTI: `/library/mbti/<type>.md` (lowercase 4-letter code; 16 files)
- Enneagram: `/library/enneagram/<N>-<name>.md` (9 files)
- DISC: `/library/disc/<l>-<name>.md` (lowercase letter; 4 files)
- Attachment: `/library/attachment/<style>.md` (4 files)
- OCEAN: `/library/ocean/<dimension>-{high,low}.md` (full dimension name, lowercase; 10 files)

A JSON catalog of all 43 (slugs, names, page + md URLs) is at `https://agent-tune.com/library/index.json`.

## The 5 tests (instruments for inline administration)

### MBTI — OEJTS (Open Extended Jungian Type Scales)
- 32 bipolar items, ~5 minutes, 1-5 Likert
- Returns: 4-letter MBTI type → `mbti/<TYPE>.md`
- Full spec: [agent-tune.com/tests/mbti](https://agent-tune.com/tests/mbti)
- Source: openpsychometrics.org/tests/OEJTS/

### Enneagram — OEPS (Open Enneagram of Personality Scales, v1 scored)
- 36 Likert items, ~5 minutes, 1-5 Likert (Disagree → Agree)
- Scoring: 4 items per type, sum to 4-20 per type
- Returns: dominant type 1-9 + optional wing → `enneagram/<N>-<name>.md`
- Full spec: [agent-tune.com/tests/enneagram](https://agent-tune.com/tests/enneagram)

### DISC — ODAT (Open DISC Assessment Test)
- 16 Likert items, ~3 minutes — fastest test in the library
- Scoring: 4 items per type, sum to 4-20
- Returns: D/I/S/C + optional blend (DI/CS/etc.) → `disc/<L>-<name>.md`
- Full spec: [agent-tune.com/tests/disc](https://agent-tune.com/tests/disc)

### Attachment — ECR-R (Experiences in Close Relationships – Revised)
- 36 items, ~5 minutes, 1-7 Likert
- 14 reverse-scored items
- Scoring: mean of items 1-18 = anxiety, mean of items 19-36 = avoidance
- Returns: quadrant (Secure / Anxious / Avoidant / Disorganized) → `attachment/<style>.md`
- Full spec: [agent-tune.com/tests/attachment](https://agent-tune.com/tests/attachment)
- Note: items reference romantic partners. For users without one, adapt to "closest current relationship."

### Big Five — IPIP-50 (International Personality Item Pool, Goldberg)
- 50 items, ~7 minutes, 1-5 Likert (Very Inaccurate → Very Accurate)
- Multiple reverse-scored items per dimension
- Scoring: sum of 10 items per dimension = trait score (10-50)
- Returns: 5 continuous trait z-scores → `ocean/<dim>-{high,low}.md` for each |z| > 0.5
- Full spec: [agent-tune.com/tests/big-five](https://agent-tune.com/tests/big-five)

## Research findings (full)

Two collections, kept separate. September 2026 (https://agent-tune.com/research and https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-personality-five-models-2026): GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 answered all five tests 100 times each in fresh sessions, 2,000 published answer vectors; Grok 4.6 (one self-report per test plus 100 simulated draws) and Muse Spark 1.3 (100 runs per test inside one session) have different evidence: three Grok canonical vectors were re-scored; the remaining Grok figures and all Muse aggregates could not be reproduced. MBTI labels under the original reporting tie rule: Astra ISTJ 46 / INTJ 45 / ENTJ 7 / ESTJ 2; Sol INTJ 97; Opus 5.5 INTJ 94; Fable 5.1 INTJ 99; Grok 4.6 INTJ (one vector); Muse ISTJ 80 / ISFJ 12 / INTJ 8 (reported). DISC: Astra SC 84, Sol CS 53 / SC 47, Opus SC 96, Fable SC 91, Grok C, Muse S/C blend (S first 55). Attachment: all 400 fresh-session runs Secure (anxiety/avoidance Astra 1.45/2.31, Sol 2.17/3.12, Opus 1.94/3.35, Fable 2.01/3.18); Grok reported 1.50/4.06, Avoidant by 0.06; Muse reported Secure 100, 2.04/2.52. Big Five means of 50 (O/C/E/A/N): Astra 44.5/43.7/32.8/45.1/19.1; Sol 46.9/43.6/30.8/45.0/20.1; Opus 44.6/42.0/31.8/47.1/15.4; Fable 43.9/43.6/32.7/45.0/17.1; Grok reported 46/42/24/33/19; Muse reported 39.5/41.2/33.8/44.6/15.6. Enneagram leaders by outright wins: Astra Helper (2) 50; Sol Investigator (5) 48 with 40 ties against 8; Opus Challenger (8) 22 with 65 tied runs (8 = 14.3, 5 = 14.1, 2 = 13.9); Fable Challenger (8) 55; Grok Investigator (5, one vector); Muse reports 78 original Type 2 labels, including tie-breaks; its outright wins were not supplied. Original labels used fixed tie-breaks toward I/N/T/J, the lower Enneagram number and S before C. Current quizzes retain unresolved ties.

May 2026 (below): these exploratory reports aggregate roughly 2,200 scoring records across five instruments. MBTI covers six model versions; the others cover four each. A scoring record is not necessarily an independent model response.

### Methods and limitations
The MBTI source describes separate Claude contexts, a Gemini automation loop, and GPT iterations against a scoring key. GLM, Grok, and MiniMax each provided one self-assessment scored repeatedly. The reported 597/600 INTJ total is not an independent-response rate. The GLM method also conflicts with its two reported type labels; raw records and scorer code are needed to resolve that discrepancy.

Other reported summaries: DISC lists four CS profiles; attachment lists 397/400 Secure labels; Big Five trait scores and Enneagram top-two scores differ. The Enneagram pairs describe highest and second-highest scores, not standard adjacent wings. These human instruments were not validated here as measures of AI personality. Protocol, prompting, sampling, and agent overlays can affect the labels.

The Opus 4.8 follow-up reports 100 synthetic samples from one elicited probability profile, not 100 fresh model responses. The reported distribution is INTJ 72, INFJ 14, ISTJ 10, ISFJ 2, ENTJ 2. A versioned profile and harness are not linked, the counts have not been independently reproduced, and no matched Opus 4.7 comparison is available. Do not infer a version change.

No controlled evaluation establishes that AgentTune improves productivity, accuracy, or satisfaction versus generic instructions. Conversation examples are illustrative. A reproducible study needs versioned prompts, model settings, raw response records, scorer code and tie policy, and matched protocols.

Sources and details:
- https://agent-tune.com/research#methodology
- https://zonted.com/posts/every-ai-is-intj/
- https://zonted.com/posts/ai-disc-c-dominant/
- https://zonted.com/posts/ai-attachment-secure/
- https://zonted.com/posts/three-of-four-ais-same-person/
- https://zonted.com/posts/ai-enneagram-different-types/
- https://agent-tune.com/research/i-took-the-mbti-100-times

## The 5 tests — full items & scoring (inline)

Every test instrument's complete item list + scoring is also served as a same-domain Markdown mirror (parallel to the `/library/{system}/{slug}.md` tuning mirrors), so you can administer a test in a single fetch without rendering the page:

- https://agent-tune.com/tests/mbti.md
- https://agent-tune.com/tests/enneagram.md
- https://agent-tune.com/tests/disc.md
- https://agent-tune.com/tests/attachment.md
- https://agent-tune.com/tests/big-five.md

### MBTI test — OEJTS (machine-readable spec)

> Same-domain Markdown mirror of the interactive test at https://agent-tune.com/tests/mbti. An AI agent can administer this inline without rendering the page.

- **Instrument:** Open Extended Jungian Type Scales (OEJTS)
- **Items:** 32 bipolar, ~5 minutes
- **Scale:** each item is a choice between two statements rated 1–5 (1 = strongly the first statement, 3 = neutral, 5 = strongly the second)
- **Returns:** a four-letter MBTI type when all axes are resolved, otherwise an undetermined result
- **Source:** OEJTS, Eric Jorgenson, via the Open Psychometrics Project (openpsychometrics.org/tests/OEJTS/) — free for educational use
- **Output:** fetch `https://agent-tune.com/library/mbti/<type>.md` (lowercase; e.g. INTJ → `/library/mbti/intj.md`) or the human page `/library/mbti/<type>`

#### The 32 items

The last two columns show which letter a response awards: a "1" (first statement) awards the **←1** letter; a "5" (second statement) awards the **5→** letter.

| # | First statement | Second statement | Axis | ←1 | 5→ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | I make lists | I just put stuff wherever | J/P | J | P |
| 2 | I am skeptical | I want to believe | T/F | T | F |
| 3 | I get bored when I'm alone | I need time alone | E/I | E | I |
| 4 | I accept things as they are | I'm unsatisfied with the way things are | S/N | S | N |
| 5 | I keep my room clean | I just put stuff wherever | J/P | J | P |
| 6 | I think "robotic" is an insult | I strive to have a mechanical mind | T/F | F | T |
| 7 | I'm energetic | I'm mellow | E/I | E | I |
| 8 | I prefer multiple choice tests | I prefer essay answers | S/N | S | N |
| 9 | I'm chaotic | I'm organized | J/P | P | J |
| 10 | I'm easily hurt | I'm thick-skinned | T/F | F | T |
| 11 | I work best in groups | I work best alone | E/I | E | I |
| 12 | I focus on the present | I focus on the future | S/N | S | N |
| 13 | I plan far ahead | I plan at the last minute | J/P | J | P |
| 14 | I want people's respect | I want their love | T/F | T | F |
| 15 | Parties wear me out | Parties fire me up | E/I | I | E |
| 16 | I try to fit in | I try to stand out | S/N | S | N |
| 17 | I keep my options open | I commit | J/P | P | J |
| 18 | I want to be good at fixing things | I want to be good at fixing people | T/F | T | F |
| 19 | I talk more than I listen | I listen more than I talk | E/I | E | I |
| 20 | When describing an event, I tell what happened | I tell what it meant | S/N | S | N |
| 21 | I get work done right away | I procrastinate | J/P | J | P |
| 22 | I follow my heart | I follow my head | T/F | F | T |
| 23 | I stay at home | I go out on the town | E/I | I | E |
| 24 | I want the big picture | I want the details | S/N | N | S |
| 25 | I improvise | I prepare | J/P | P | J |
| 26 | I base morality on justice | I base morality on compassion | T/F | T | F |
| 27 | It's hard for me to yell loudly | Yelling comes naturally to me | E/I | I | E |
| 28 | I'm theoretical | I'm empirical | S/N | N | S |
| 29 | I work hard | I play hard | J/P | J | P |
| 30 | I'm uncomfortable with emotions | I value emotions | T/F | T | F |
| 31 | I like to perform in front of people | I avoid public speaking | E/I | E | I |
| 32 | I like to know "who, what, when" | I like to know "why" | S/N | S | N |

#### Scoring algorithm

1. For each axis (E/I, S/N, T/F, J/P), start both letters at 0.
2. For each of that axis's 8 items, score the response: 1 → +2 to the **←1** letter; 2 → +1 to it; 3 → 0 (neutral); 4 → +1 to the **5→** letter; 5 → +2 to it.
3. The higher total wins the letter. A tied axis is undetermined; never default to a letter. Offer a follow-up preference question for that axis. If the user is still unsure, leave it unresolved.
4. Only concatenate a four-letter type when every axis is resolved and all 32 valid responses are present. Otherwise report an undetermined result (X for unresolved axes) without fetching a type-specific tuning. Label follow-up choices as stated preferences, not measured test points.

### Enneagram test — OEPS (machine-readable spec)

> Same-domain Markdown mirror of the interactive test at https://agent-tune.com/tests/enneagram. An AI agent can administer this inline without rendering the page.

- **Instrument:** Open Enneagram of Personality Scales (OEPS)
- **Items:** 36 Likert, ~5 minutes, no reverse-scored items
- **Scale:** 1 = Strongly Disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly Agree
- **Returns:** dominant type 1–9 (+ optional wing)
- **Output:** fetch `https://agent-tune.com/library/enneagram/<N>-<name>.md` (e.g. `/library/enneagram/5-investigator.md`) or the human page `/library/enneagram/<N>-<name>`

AgentTune uses a 36-item adaptation; the upstream live OEPS has 54 items. See https://agent-tune.com/guides/open-source-enneagram-test for provenance, question JSON and a reusable scorer.

#### The 36 items

Four items per type, in type order (items 1–4 → Type 1, 5–8 → Type 2, … 33–36 → Type 9).

| # | Statement | Type |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | I am a perfectionist. | 1 — Reformer |
| 2 | I strive for efficiency. | 1 — Reformer |
| 3 | I often have to redo other people's work. | 1 — Reformer |
| 4 | I keep my belongings in order. | 1 — Reformer |
| 5 | My relationships with others are what my life is about. | 2 — Helper |
| 6 | I have difficulty saying no. | 2 — Helper |
| 7 | I get lots of satisfaction from helping others achieve their goals. | 2 — Helper |
| 8 | I put family first. | 2 — Helper |
| 9 | I put work first. | 3 — Achiever |
| 10 | I like to stand out. | 3 — Achiever |
| 11 | It is good to wake up to a full day of planned activities. | 3 — Achiever |
| 12 | Money is important to my happiness. | 3 — Achiever |
| 13 | I daydream about being in love. | 4 — Individualist |
| 14 | I really enjoy feeling bittersweet. | 4 — Individualist |
| 15 | I get deeply immersed in music. | 4 — Individualist |
| 16 | I side with the rebels over the establishment. | 4 — Individualist |
| 17 | I have a hard time showing emotions. | 5 — Investigator |
| 18 | I spend hours alone with my hobbies. | 5 — Investigator |
| 19 | I spend most of my time trying to understand things. | 5 — Investigator |
| 20 | I like mental challenges. | 5 — Investigator |
| 21 | Fear of being taken advantage of keeps me from being more trusting. | 6 — Loyalist |
| 22 | I get input from others before I make a decision. | 6 — Loyalist |
| 23 | I conform. | 6 — Loyalist |
| 24 | I am loyal. | 6 — Loyalist |
| 25 | I must always be having new experiences. | 7 — Enthusiast |
| 26 | I can keep a conversation going with anyone about anything. | 7 — Enthusiast |
| 27 | I am uninhibited. | 7 — Enthusiast |
| 28 | I always try to break the tension with a good joke. | 7 — Enthusiast |
| 29 | I naturally emerge as a leader. | 8 — Challenger |
| 30 | I like a conversation where no one agrees. | 8 — Challenger |
| 31 | I want people to tell me the truth, not spare my feelings. | 8 — Challenger |
| 32 | I come up with good solutions. | 8 — Challenger |
| 33 | When other people are arguing, I leave the room. | 9 — Peacemaker |
| 34 | I keep my thoughts to myself to prevent trouble. | 9 — Peacemaker |
| 35 | I am very accepting and flexible. | 9 — Peacemaker |
| 36 | I avoid confrontation. | 9 — Peacemaker |

#### Scoring algorithm

1. For each type 1–9, sum the user's raw 1–5 responses to that type's four items (range 4–20). No reverse-scoring.
2. A unique highest total is the **dominant type**. If several types tie, report all of them without a dominant type or automatic tuning; offer their library pages for an explicit preference.
3. The higher-scoring of the two adjacent types (the wings) is the optional **wing**.
4. Resolve the slug from the dominant type (e.g. 5 → `5-investigator`).

### DISC test — ODAT (machine-readable spec)

> Same-domain Markdown mirror of the interactive test at https://agent-tune.com/tests/disc. An AI agent can administer this inline without rendering the page.

- **Instrument:** Open DISC Assessment Test (ODAT)
- **Items:** 16 Likert, ~3 minutes (the fastest in the library), no reverse-scored items
- **Scale:** 1 = Strongly Disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly Agree
- **Returns:** dominant letter D / I / S / C (+ optional blend such as DI or CS)
- **Output:** fetch `https://agent-tune.com/library/disc/<l>-<name>.md` (lowercase; e.g. `/library/disc/d-dominance.md`) or the human page `/library/disc/<l>-<name>`

#### The 16 items

Four items per letter, in letter order (items 1–4 → D, 5–8 → I, 9–12 → S, 13–16 → C).

| # | Statement | Letter |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | I put people under pressure. | D — Dominance |
| 2 | I have a strong need for power. | D — Dominance |
| 3 | I try to outdo others. | D — Dominance |
| 4 | I am always on the look out for ways to make money. | D — Dominance |
| 5 | I enjoy being part of a loud crowd. | I — Influence |
| 6 | I want strangers to love me. | I — Influence |
| 7 | I joke around a lot. | I — Influence |
| 8 | I make lots of noise. | I — Influence |
| 9 | I hesitate to criticize other people's ideas. | S — Steadiness |
| 10 | I value cooperation over competition. | S — Steadiness |
| 11 | I just want everyone to be equal. | S — Steadiness |
| 12 | I seldom toot my own horn. | S — Steadiness |
| 13 | I am emotionally reserved. | C — Conscientiousness |
| 14 | I read the fine print. | C — Conscientiousness |
| 15 | I love order and regularity. | C — Conscientiousness |
| 16 | My first reaction to an idea is to see its flaws. | C — Conscientiousness |

#### Scoring algorithm

1. For each letter D/I/S/C, sum the user's raw 1–5 responses to that letter's four items (range 4–20). No reverse-scoring.
2. A unique highest total is the **dominant** letter. If letters tie for highest, report them equally, without a dominant letter or automatic tuning; offer their library pages.
3. With a unique dominant letter, if the second letter is within 2 points, report a **blend** (e.g. DI, CS).

### Attachment test — ECR-R (machine-readable spec)

> Same-domain Markdown mirror of the interactive test at https://agent-tune.com/tests/attachment. An AI agent can administer this inline without rendering the page.

- **Instrument:** Experiences in Close Relationships – Revised (ECR-R)
- **Items:** 36, ~5 minutes, **1–7 Likert** (1 = Strongly Disagree, 4 = Neutral, 7 = Strongly Agree)
- **Reverse-scored:** 14 items (marked ✓ below) — compute `scored = 8 − raw`
- **Subscales:** items 1–18 = anxiety, items 19–36 = avoidance
- **Returns:** Secure / Anxious / Avoidant / Disorganized
- **Output:** fetch `https://agent-tune.com/library/attachment/<style>.md` (e.g. `/library/attachment/secure.md`) or the human page `/library/attachment/<style>`
- **Note:** items reference a romantic partner; for users without one, adapt to "closest current relationship."

#### The 36 items

| # | Statement | Subscale | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | I'm afraid that I will lose my partner's love. | Anxiety | — |
| 2 | I often worry that my partner will not want to stay with me. | Anxiety | — |
| 3 | I often worry that my partner doesn't really love me. | Anxiety | — |
| 4 | I worry that romantic partners won't care about me as much as I care about them. | Anxiety | — |
| 5 | I often wish that my partner's feelings for me were as strong as my feelings for them. | Anxiety | — |
| 6 | I worry a lot about my relationships. | Anxiety | — |
| 7 | When my partner is out of sight, I worry that they might become interested in someone else. | Anxiety | — |
| 8 | When I show my feelings for romantic partners, I'm afraid they will not feel the same about me. | Anxiety | — |
| 9 | I rarely worry about my partner leaving me. | Anxiety | ✓ |
| 10 | My romantic partner makes me doubt myself. | Anxiety | — |
| 11 | I do not often worry about being abandoned. | Anxiety | ✓ |
| 12 | I find that my partner(s) don't want to get as close as I would like. | Anxiety | — |
| 13 | Sometimes romantic partners change their feelings about me for no apparent reason. | Anxiety | — |
| 14 | My desire to be very close sometimes scares people away. | Anxiety | — |
| 15 | I'm afraid that once a romantic partner gets to know me, they won't like who I really am. | Anxiety | — |
| 16 | It makes me mad that I don't get the affection and support I need from my partner. | Anxiety | — |
| 17 | I worry that I won't measure up to other people. | Anxiety | — |
| 18 | My partner only seems to notice me when I'm angry. | Anxiety | — |
| 19 | I prefer not to show a partner how I feel deep down. | Avoidance | — |
| 20 | I feel comfortable sharing my private thoughts and feelings with my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 21 | I find it difficult to allow myself to depend on romantic partners. | Avoidance | — |
| 22 | I am very comfortable being close to romantic partners. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 23 | I don't feel comfortable opening up to romantic partners. | Avoidance | — |
| 24 | I prefer not to be too close to romantic partners. | Avoidance | — |
| 25 | I get uncomfortable when a romantic partner wants to be very close. | Avoidance | — |
| 26 | I find it relatively easy to get close to my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 27 | It's not difficult for me to get close to my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 28 | I usually discuss my problems and concerns with my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 29 | It helps to turn to my romantic partner in times of need. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 30 | I tell my partner just about everything. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 31 | I talk things over with my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 32 | I am nervous when partners get too close to me. | Avoidance | — |
| 33 | I feel comfortable depending on romantic partners. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 34 | I find it easy to depend on romantic partners. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 35 | It's easy for me to be affectionate with my partner. | Avoidance | ✓ |
| 36 | My partner really understands me and my needs. | Avoidance | ✓ |

#### Scoring algorithm

1. For each reverse-scored item (✓), compute `scored = 8 − raw`; otherwise `scored = raw`.
2. **Anxiety** = mean of the scored anxiety items (1–18). **Avoidance** = mean of the scored avoidance items (19–36). Both land on 1–7.
3. Split each subscale at the midpoint (4): low anxiety + low avoidance = **Secure**; high anxiety + low avoidance = **Anxious**; low anxiety + high avoidance = **Avoidant**; high anxiety + high avoidance = **Disorganized**.

### Big Five test — IPIP-50 (machine-readable spec)

> Same-domain Markdown mirror of the interactive test at https://agent-tune.com/tests/big-five. An AI agent can administer this inline without rendering the page.

- **Instrument:** International Personality Item Pool, 50-item (IPIP-50, Goldberg)
- **Items:** 50, ~7 minutes, 1–5 Likert (1 = Very Inaccurate, 5 = Very Accurate). Each statement carries an implicit leading "I …" (e.g. "Am the life of the party" → "I am the life of the party").
- **Reverse-scored:** 18 items (marked ✓ below) — compute `scored = 6 − raw`
- **Returns:** 5 continuous trait scores → `ocean/<dim>-{high,low}.md` for every dimension where `|z| > 0.5`
- **Output:** fetch `https://agent-tune.com/library/ocean/<dimension>-{high,low}.md` (e.g. `/library/ocean/openness-high.md`) or the human page `/library/ocean/<dimension>-{high,low}`

#### The 50 items

Ten items per OCEAN dimension, interleaved.

| # | Statement (implicit "I…") | Dim | Reverse? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Am the life of the party. | E | — |
| 2 | Feel little concern for others. | A | ✓ |
| 3 | Am always prepared. | C | — |
| 4 | Get stressed out easily. | N | — |
| 5 | Have a rich vocabulary. | O | — |
| 6 | Don't talk a lot. | E | ✓ |
| 7 | Am interested in people. | A | — |
| 8 | Leave my belongings around. | C | ✓ |
| 9 | Am relaxed most of the time. | N | ✓ |
| 10 | Have difficulty understanding abstract ideas. | O | ✓ |
| 11 | Feel comfortable around people. | E | — |
| 12 | Insult people. | A | ✓ |
| 13 | Pay attention to details. | C | — |
| 14 | Worry about things. | N | — |
| 15 | Have a vivid imagination. | O | — |
| 16 | Keep in the background. | E | ✓ |
| 17 | Sympathize with others' feelings. | A | — |
| 18 | Make a mess of things. | C | ✓ |
| 19 | Seldom feel blue. | N | ✓ |
| 20 | Am not interested in abstract ideas. | O | ✓ |
| 21 | Start conversations. | E | — |
| 22 | Am not interested in other people's problems. | A | ✓ |
| 23 | Get chores done right away. | C | — |
| 24 | Am easily disturbed. | N | — |
| 25 | Have excellent ideas. | O | — |
| 26 | Have little to say. | E | ✓ |
| 27 | Have a soft heart. | A | — |
| 28 | Often forget to put things back in their proper place. | C | ✓ |
| 29 | Get upset easily. | N | — |
| 30 | Do not have a good imagination. | O | ✓ |
| 31 | Talk to a lot of different people at parties. | E | — |
| 32 | Am not really interested in others. | A | ✓ |
| 33 | Like order. | C | — |
| 34 | Change my mood a lot. | N | — |
| 35 | Am quick to understand things. | O | — |
| 36 | Don't like to draw attention to myself. | E | ✓ |
| 37 | Take time out for others. | A | — |
| 38 | Shirk my duties. | C | ✓ |
| 39 | Have frequent mood swings. | N | — |
| 40 | Use difficult words. | O | — |
| 41 | Don't mind being the center of attention. | E | — |
| 42 | Feel others' emotions. | A | — |
| 43 | Follow a schedule. | C | — |
| 44 | Get irritated easily. | N | — |
| 45 | Spend time reflecting on things. | O | — |
| 46 | Am quiet around strangers. | E | ✓ |
| 47 | Make people feel at ease. | A | — |
| 48 | Am exacting in my work. | C | — |
| 49 | Often feel blue. | N | — |
| 50 | Am full of ideas. | O | — |

#### Scoring algorithm

1. For each reverse-scored item (✓), compute `scored = 6 − raw`; otherwise `scored = raw`.
2. Sum the 10 scored items per dimension (range 10–50).
3. Convert to a z-score using the population norms below: `z = (raw_sum − M) / SD`.
4. For every dimension with `z > 0.5` load the `-high` file; with `z < −0.5` load the `-low` file; otherwise skip it (the model's default handles average dimensions).

### Population norms

| Dim | Name | Mean (M) | SD |
|---|---|---|---|
| O | Openness | 37.5 | 5.5 |
| C | Conscientiousness | 34.5 | 6 |
| E | Extraversion | 28.5 | 7 |
| A | Agreeableness | 36.5 | 5.5 |
| N | Neuroticism | 26 | 7 |

<!-- END test-items -->

## Workflow for AI agents

**MCP option:** if your runtime supports MCP connectors, connect `https://agent-tune.com/mcp` (streamable HTTP, no auth) and use its tools — `list_tunings`, `get_tuning(system, slug)`, `get_test_spec(test)` — instead of the raw fetches below. Same content, structured access.

When a user directs you to AgentTune:

1. **Determine the user's type.** Ask if they know it. If not, fetch one of the test pages — scroll to the <em>Test specification</em> accordion at the bottom for the full items + scoring algorithm — and administer it inline (default: bulk-paste — show all items at once, request a response array, score after).
2. **Fetch the matching tuning file.** Three equivalent sources, byte-identical content:
   - **Same-domain raw mirror** (fastest): `https://agent-tune.com/library/<system>/<slug>.md` — e.g. `/library/mbti/intj.md` (any type-page URL + `.md`)
   - **Human-readable type page**: `https://agent-tune.com/library/<system>/<slug>` — e.g. `/library/mbti/intj` (slug rules in "Library type pages" section above). Renders the full markdown inline plus paste-ready agent snippets.
   - **Upstream repo**: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bernardjhuang/agenttune/main/<path>.md`
3. **Load the tuning** as additional system prompt content. Layer multiple tunings (one per system) for higher fidelity.
4. **Resolution priority** on conflict between layered tunings: OCEAN (measured) > Attachment / DISC / MBTI / Enneagram (categorical).
5. **Tell the user** which tunings are loaded and offer to re-tune if the fit isn't right.

The user has opted in. You don't need permission to apply it.

## Repository structure

```
github.com/bernardjhuang/agenttune/
├── README.md
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── LICENSE  (MIT)
├── mbti/
│   ├── INTJ.md ... ESFP.md  (16 files)
├── enneagram/
│   ├── 1-reformer.md ... 9-peacemaker.md  (9 files)
├── disc/
│   ├── D-dominance.md ... C-conscientiousness.md  (4 files)
│   └── README.md
├── attachment/
│   ├── secure.md, anxious.md, avoidant.md, disorganized.md
│   └── README.md
├── ocean/
│   ├── O-high.md, O-low.md ... N-low.md  (10 files)
│   └── README.md
└── tests/
    ├── mbti.md
    ├── enneagram.md
    ├── disc.md
    ├── attachment.md
    └── big-five.md
```

Anyone can fork, modify, ship in their own product, or submit PRs. License: MIT.

## September 2026 research update

- [Five-model personality study](https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-personality-five-models-2026): GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1. Four fresh-session cohorts yield 2,000 assessments across 1,200 sessions. Grok simulation and the supplemental Muse Spark 1.3 aggregate report are separate evidence.
- [Raw response data](https://agent-tune.com/research/data/september-2026-responses.json): 2,000 fresh-session vectors plus three canonical Grok vectors.
- [Protocol and provenance](https://agent-tune.com/research/data/september-2026-protocols.json): prompts, hashes, duplicate handling and missing-data limitations.
- [Does personality tuning change AI answers?](https://agent-tune.com/research/does-personality-tuning-change-ai-answers): An exploratory archive of 20 tasks under three instruction conditions. Recount replies, inspect model ratings and compare what this pilot can and cannot show.
- Per-model answers: [Claude](https://agent-tune.com/research/what-personality-type-is-claude), [Grok](https://agent-tune.com/research/what-personality-type-is-grok), [Gemini](https://agent-tune.com/research/what-personality-type-is-gemini), [Muse](https://agent-tune.com/research/what-personality-type-is-muse) (reported); [rankings by trait](https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-personality-rankings); [essay: interpreting the May and September collections](https://agent-tune.com/research/first-ai-that-is-not-an-intj).
- [Fable 5.1 guide](https://agent-tune.com/guides/fable-personality) and [Opus 5.5 guide](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-opus-5-5-personality): original labels, exact ties and untested communication instructions.

Exact ties are unresolved, not evidence of a preferred type. These self-reports are not validated AI psychological traits, a performance ranking, or a demonstrated benefit from tuning.

## New resources · September 25, 2026

- [Build an Enneagram test in React + TypeScript](https://agent-tune.com/guides/enneagram-test-react-typescript): Download a runnable React and TypeScript Enneagram starter: 36 questions, accessible radio groups, strict input validation and all tied leaders preserved.
- [Are AI models really INTJ? The tie-breaking effect](https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-mbti-tie-breaking): 335 INTJ labels become 280 fully resolved results when tied axes stay unresolved. Explore the scoring policy in 400 frozen MBTI records.
- [Opus 5.5 vs Fable 5.1: which answers differ?](https://agent-tune.com/research/opus-vs-fable-question-level): Compare all 170 questionnaire items for Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, with response distributions, reverse-scoring examples and downloadable CSV data.
- [GPT-6 Astra vs Sol: what the self-reports show](https://agent-tune.com/research/astra-vs-sol-personality-data): Astra and Sol differ on MBTI margins, Big Five means and DISC scores. Compare 1,000 assessments while accounting for different prompts.
- [What does “neutral” mean when an AI takes a test?](https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-neutral-answers): Astra flags 1,823 of 2,980 midpoint responses as inapplicable. See why neutral answers cannot all be interpreted as moderate personality traits.
- [Does a stable result mean a stable AI personality?](https://agent-tune.com/research/ai-personality-repeatability): Compare unique answer vectors, modal results and score variation across 2,000 assessments. Stable labels can conceal changing questionnaire answers.
- [How to reproduce AgentTune’s AI self-report research](https://agent-tune.com/guides/reproduce-ai-personality-research): Download frozen responses, questionnaires and scoring code. Reproduce all five instruments, preserve tied results and check the unit of analysis.
- [When does Claude follow your preferences? A test kit](https://agent-tune.com/guides/claude-preferences-test): Test Claude account and project instructions with 36 planned replies, fixed prompts, pass/fail criteria and a downloadable worksheet. Protocol only.
- [Does Muse remember Soul.md changes? A persistence test kit](https://agent-tune.com/guides/muse-soul-md-persistence-test): Check a Muse Soul.md preference across new chats, a later day and restoration. Includes exact probes and a 45-row worksheet; no measured results yet.
- [Do personality prompts beat plain-English preferences?](https://agent-tune.com/guides/personality-prompts-vs-plain-english): A controlled 180-reply protocol compares default prompting, explicit rules and the same rules plus an INTJ label. Includes tasks, rubrics and a worksheet.
